method.label: Find and count the repeating cycle

annotationRationale: The solution verifies a cycle of repeated operations and uses the remainder after division by its length to locate the final value.
sourceMethod: Follows the official iteration-and-cycle method. Counts the remaining operations from the first occurrence of 20 to make the cycle indexing explicit.

review.mathCheck: Six operations take 100 to 20. The verified cycle is 20→30→10→20. Since 100−6=94=31×3+1, the remaining operations give 30, choice C. The operation remains defined on positive integers throughout.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful adaptation of MAA Solution 10 on page 5. Subtracting the six-operation transient is equivalent to the official indexing by residues modulo 3.
review.annotationCheck: Both assessed nodes are used directly: verifying repeated iteration and locating the final value by a remainder. No additional recurrence node is necessary.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: Neither selected competition node has an accepted CN link. The packet establishes no national alignment for the cycle-and-remainder method.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: Neither selected node has an accepted US link. Retaining the competition skills without assigning a nearby sequence standard is appropriate.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The iteration node fits verification of the three-step cycle. The congruence/remainder node fits elementary remainder indexing; modular sums, products, and general composition-domain calculations are not demonstrated.
